invariants: The project repository owns current planning, design, structured data, approved runtime assets, code, scenes, resources, tests, and validation evidence for its domains.
ChatGPT Work is an execution surface and ChatGPT Library is reference storage; neither replaces repository paths, diffs, commits, or exact SHA authority.
AI and Codex continuity is carried by repository Markdown, JSON, manifests, implementation files, tests, and handoffs rather than chat history or memory.
New Notion writes are not required by default. Existing Notion content may be read only to discover and migrate unique project information.
A project remains in LEGACY_READ_ONLY migration state until all three migration exit counters are zero and readback evidence is recorded.
Codex rehydrates the current project at an exact repository SHA before product mutation and does not assume chat or PDF state is newer than the repository.
An approved visual consumed by the product resolves to a project-controlled repository path, SHA-256 value, actual consumer, approval state, implementation state, and provenance record.
A generated or uploaded visual is not implementation-ready merely because it appears in chat, Library, a PDF, or a preview; the approved binary and manifest readback are required.
Human PDF review, document generation, static tests, and repository write success are distinct from runtime PASS, UX PASS, player PASS, and release PASS.
Notion retirement does not require destructive deletion. Historical workspaces may remain read-only for audit and rollback.
A project-specific Notion exception requires explicit user approval, a recorded scope and owner, a measurable value unavailable from the repository-first path, and an exit or revisit condition.
Google Sheets, Figma, HTML dashboards, ChatGPT Work, ChatGPT Library, and legacy Notion pages are not parallel project canon unless an explicit project-specific contract says otherwise.
Every L1+ project task observes the latest completed Base main before selecting an execution revision; a stored Base pin is evidence of adoption or execution and is not a freshness bypass.
The latest completed Base main does not silently replace project canon, approved decisions, actual implementation, or the project's adopted Base contract.

The selected Base execution SHA remains fixed for one bounded task or play-meaningful Slice; a later relevant Base change requires impact classification, reconciliation, and affected revalidation before the execution pin changes.
Implementation handoff, pre-merge, post-merge, and closeout each require a new Base freshness read and drift classification without converting execution into a floating latest reference.

The two-artifact Blueprint profile uses a structural first-pass revision before required image and material preparation and a final second-pass revision after candidate review; both passes remain revisions inside the same PDF and AI Markdown artifact boundary rather than additional canon.

When a valid predecessor Blueprint exists, the successor is produced by incremental revision and may not silently omit stable IDs, approved decisions, explanatory sections, diagrams, approved assets, consumer links, or evidence.

Every removal, replacement, rename, or evidence-status downgrade between predecessor and successor requires an explicit semantic-delta reason, replacement or supersession reference when applicable, and verification-impact record.
If the predecessor Blueprint or its source cannot be read reliably, the task fails closed as BLOCKED_UNVERIFIED instead of rebuilding missing facts from chat history, memory, or inference.

Project, goal, system, and case completion counts include only evidence-backed PASS or DONE states and preserve separate documented, implemented, automated-test, runtime, UX, and user-approval dimensions.
Project authority is federated: the repository execution/data canon and a user-approved, manifest-registered human Blueprint PDF canon own separate domains under one editable owner per atomic fact.
The repository canon owns editable code, scenes, resources, assets, structured data, identifiers, rules, values, state transitions, decisions, work status, tests, runtime facts, and evidence.

The approved human Blueprint PDF canon owns the immutable user-reviewed visual hierarchy, project/player experience map, flow composition, information priority, milestone scope presentation, and human review baseline.
A generated candidate, preview, Library-only PDF, or PDF annotation is not canon and cannot mutate repository-owned structured facts.
PDF structured content and progress status are repository projections; project_work_kanban remains the single mutable progress source.

PDF canon activation requires user approval, exact source commit, PDF SHA-256, approval reference, approval time, canonical status, supersession reference, and repository-controlled manifest reference.
An approved PDF is immutable; a correction creates a new version and hash while preserving superseded approval history.
A structured mismatch requires repository-owner reconciliation and PDF regeneration; an approved visual-baseline mismatch requires implementation correction or a newly approved PDF.
CANON_CONFLICT blocks completion and release until repository and approved-PDF domains are reconciled.
The original V4 effective date is preserved; the federated dual-canon authority amendment is effective 2026-09-04 under the recorded user approval reference.
Codex and GPT Work read the approved PDF canon manifest, locator, source commit, approval reference, canonical status, and PDF SHA-256 before using its visual/review baseline.
Canonical PDF storage uses a project-controlled repository path or governed GitHub Release locator whose hash and supersession history are registered in the repository manifest.

The dual-canon contract does not trigger mass project backfill; a project adopts it through explicit synchronization or its next Blueprint revision while preserving its currently adopted contract until then.
